stories.title: BGP Delegation Meets Assam CM, Donates Rs 2.34 Lakh to CMRF for Flood Relief in Sivasagar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: A delegation of the Bharatiya Gorkha Parisangh (BGP), Assam State Committee, led by its Chief Advisor and Immediate former President, Shri Amar Adhikari, called on the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Assam at Lokseva Bhawan, the Chief Minister’s Office at the Assam Secretariat, Guwahati, on 5th November.

The delegation was accompanied by BGP National President Shri Nityananda Upadhyay and National General Secretary (Administration) Shri Nanda Kirati Dewan, who also serves as the Chief Spokesperson of the BGP Assam State Committee.

The delegation held an elaborate discussion with the Chief Minister regarding the memorandum submitted by the Bharatiya Gorkha Parisangh seeking recognition of the Gorkha community of Assam as Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (OTFDs) under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006.

Himanta Biswa Sarma gave a patient hearing to the delegation and informed them that the Government of Assam had already undertaken the necessary steps within its jurisdiction following the receipt of the memorandum submitted by the Bharatiya Gorkha Parisangh through email last year.

He stated that the matter now rests with the Government of India, particularly concerning the appropriate nomenclature and the consideration of Gorkhas under the category of Other Traditional Forest Dwellers or forest-dependent communities.
He further clarified that the State Government could consider the matter further based on the relevant directions and legal provisions received from the Government of India.
In this regard, the Chief Minister advised the Bharatiya Gorkha Parisangh to pursue the matter with the Central Government for appropriate consideration and necessary action.

Speaking to this correspondent, Nanda Kirati Dewan stated that the historical association of the Gorkha community with forests in Assam formed the basis of its demand for recognition under the Forest Rights Act.

“Gorkhas, who were historically identified as Nepali graziers and cultivators, constituted a forest-dependent community and were accorded the status of Special Protected Class under Chapter X of the Assam Land and Revenue Regulations, 1886.
Even today, the descendants continue to reside in Reserve Forests and Forest Villages and remain dependent on forest resources for their livelihood.

Therefore, the legitimate rights of eligible Gorkhas residing in such areas, including entitlement to Forest Rights Certificates (FRCs), must be considered in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Forest Rights Act, 2006,” Dewan stated.

He further said that the Bharatiya Gorkha Parisangh had initiated the process and was committed to pursuing the matter to its logical conclusion through representations and interventions at all appropriate levels of governance.

stories.headline: India's investment outlook strengthens
stories.title: India's investment outlook strengthens
stories.summary: New Delhi: India's investment outlook is strengthening as accelerating credit growth and rising corporate revenues point to stronger private capital spending, while a possible cooling of global energy prices could ease pressure on company margins, according to an HSBC report.The report, titled "Why so down on India?" and dated November 6, said the economy's resilience warranted a reassessment of concerns surrounding higher energy costs and the impact of artificial intelligence on services exports.Also Read: India's invisible pain: The dirt in the air comes with a hefty price tag for economy and businesses"Accelerating credit growth, for example, hints at stronger investment spending to come, including by private firms that have for years lagged in the capex cycle," the report said.Funds flowing to the commercial sector increased to 6.6 per cent of GDP during April-September 2026 from 4.7 per cent a year earlier. Credit growth to larger companies, which typically undertake major capital expenditure projects, accelerated particularly strongly, while smaller businesses also increased borrowing.Also Read: States' capital outlay to accelerate to 10-12% on Centre support in FY27, urban infra to lead: CrisilCorporate revenue growth moved above its trend over the past decade in both nominal and real terms, supporting the case for further investment despite rising interest rates.HSBC said almost 70 per cent of around 100 growth indicators tracked by its India economics team signalled expansion in the latest quarter, compared with just under 55 per cent in the second quarter.The report also pointed to scope for foreign direct investment to recover, supported by continued growth, reforms and expanding data centre investment."But there are reasons to be optimistic about net FDI drifting higher again: continued growth and reforms in India are bound to lure companies back again," it said.However, data centre investment could temporarily increase imports of expensive equipment, the report noted.On the external front, rising services exports helped cushion the economy against the oil price shock, keeping the current account deficit narrow and steady. A recent acceleration in goods exports, despite largely stalled global trade in non-AI goods, suggested India was gradually gaining market share.Government infrastructure spending remained another support, with central capital expenditure exceeding 3 per cent of GDP annually, compared with less than 2 per cent before COVID-19.HSBC nevertheless flagged weak rural demand following rainfall shortages and repeated heatwaves, alongside inflation pressures hurting households and squeezing corporate margins."In fact, a cooling of global energy prices in the coming months could offer considerable relief," the report said.Its India economics team also expected consumer price inflation to stabilise, although a quick reversal was not assured.

opening: New Delhi: India's investment outlook is strengthening as accelerating credit growth and rising corporate revenues point to stronger private capital spending, while a possible cooling of global energy prices could ease pressure on company margins, according to an HSBC report.

The report, titled "Why so down on India?" and dated November 6, said the economy's resilience warranted a reassessment of concerns surrounding higher energy costs and the impact of artificial intelligence on services exports." Accelerating credit growth, for example, hints at stronger investment spending to come, including by private firms that have for years lagged in the capex cycle," the report said.
body: Funds flowing to the commercial sector increased to 6.6 per cent of GDP during April-September 2026 from 4.7 per cent a year earlier.
Credit growth to larger companies, which typically undertake major capital expenditure projects, accelerated particularly strongly, while smaller businesses also increased borrowing.
Corporate revenue growth moved above its trend over the past decade in both nominal and real terms, supporting the case for further investment despite rising interest rates.
HSBC said almost 70 per cent of around 100 growth indicators tracked by its India economics team signalled expansion in the latest quarter, compared with just under 55 per cent in the second quarter.

The report also pointed to scope for foreign direct investment to recover, supported by continued growth, reforms and expanding data centre investment." But there are reasons to be optimistic about net FDI drifting higher again: continued growth and reforms in India are bound to lure companies back again," it said.
However, data centre investment could temporarily increase imports of expensive equipment, the report noted.
On the external front, rising services exports helped cushion the economy against the oil price shock, keeping the current account deficit narrow and steady.
A recent acceleration in goods exports, despite largely stalled global trade in non-AI goods, suggested India was gradually gaining market share.
Government infrastructure spending remained another support, with central capital expenditure exceeding 3 per cent of GDP annually, compared with less than 2 per cent before COVID-19.

HSBC nevertheless flagged weak rural demand following rainfall shortages and repeated heatwaves, alongside inflation pressures hurting households and squeezing corporate margins." In fact, a cooling of global energy prices in the coming months could offer considerable relief," the report said.
Its India economics team also expected consumer price inflation to stabilise, although a quick reversal was not assured.

HSBC said almost 70 per cent of around 100 growth indicators tracked by its India economics team signalled expansion in the latest quarter, compared with just under 55 per cent in the second quarter.
Government infrastructure spending remained another support, with central capital expenditure exceeding 3 per cent of GDP annually, compared with less than 2 per cent before COVID-19.

stories.headline: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
stories.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
stories.summary: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index.

Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also expressed concern over “bumper-to-bumper” traffic in Delhi-NCR.
“We keep talking and sometimes make statements and suggestions, but the point is that AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI said.
The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad.
“Look at the roads in Delhi and the roads connecting Delhi with the NCR.
Take a look at any road and the kind of vehicles moving on it.
That is the major problem,” the CJI said.
The Bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood.
On stubble burning, the Bench stressed the need to educate farmers about using machines instead of resorting to farm fires.

On the plea seeking closure of schools or running them in hybrid mode for students of all age groups if the air quality index (AQI) rises above a certain mark, the bench said it will go by experts’ opinion.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, referred to the regulatory framework covering five major sectors: industrial emissions, vehicular pollution, construction and demolition dust, road dust and stubble burning.

She told the Bench that several measures had been introduced, including restrictions on the entry of certain vehicles, geo-tagging of pollution under control (PUC) certificates and action against visibly polluting vehicles through complaints received on applications and social media.

The Times reported last month that US intelligence agencies had discovered that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, was feeding information directly to China."I love our country and our company. opening: Nvidia shares fell more than 4% in overnight trading on Monday after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having a close relationship with a business executive reportedly alleged by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
The reports have prompted the company to launch an investigation.
body: Nvidia shares dropped to $178 apiece overnight.
This came after Huang in a message to company employees released on Sunday acknowledged having an affair and apologised to both his family and company staff.
"I was unfaithful to my wife.
My actions hurt her and our children.
There is no excuse for what I did.
I am deeply sorry,” the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born executive said." Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life.
My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust.
I have fallen short of that responsibility,” he further wrote in the letter to employees obtained by The Associated Press.
Also read | Nvidia probes CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: Here’s the lowdown.
Who is Alice Huang?

Why the personal matter of the CEO may have spooked investors is because the person he has been intimate with is Alice Huang, who previously was a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.

The Times reported last month that US intelligence agencies had discovered that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, was feeding information directly to China." I love our country and our company.
I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security,” Jensen Huang said.

Nvidia meanwhile launched the investigation into reports that the CEO was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.
Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," the board said.
Huang will continue to hold the position of CEO during the investigation.
Also read | Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?
Donald Trump, Musk back Nvidia CEOUS President Donald Trump said he thinks Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is an honourable guy.
“I have not spoken to him about it.
I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on.
I hope everything's fine,” he said.
Sequoia Capital partner Shaun Maguire described Huang as "one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation", while acknowledging that the Nvidia chief had made a serious mistake.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk reacted to Maguire's post with a brief endorsement, saying: "I agree." Billionaire Bill Ackman said Huang has done a lot of good for the world and he hopes the damage here is minimal.
“That is, I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security,” he said.
“I am not suggesting he gets a free pass.
If indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.” What lies ahead for Nvidia shares?
This boardroom storm at Nvidia has landed at a brutal time for the AI trade, but Nvidia's earnings on November 17 are the real next test, Reuters quoted Etoro lead analyst Josh Gilbert as saying.

While the investigation is likely to dent sentiment, it won't alter anything long-term unless it leads to a change at the top, at which point it becomes a completely different ball game, the analyst said.
Will Huang get replaced?
Pepperstone Head of Research Chris Weston doesn’t think so.
“I think given that he is like the godfather of AI and, you know, the OG of what has been the biggest investment thematic that we've seen in a generation,” Reuters quoted him as saying.
If things went south and Huang had to step down, then Nvidia shares may see an absolute bloodbath, according to the analyst.

stories.headline: The Man Saving Kashmir's Dying Lakes | Manzoor Wangnoo - Green Ambassador of Kashmir
stories.title: The Man Saving Kashmir's Dying Lakes | Manzoor Wangnoo - Green Ambassador of Kashmir
stories.summary: He was mentioned by PM Modi in Mann Ki Baat. They call him the Green Ambassador of Kashmir. But today, he is fighting alone. This is Manzoor Wangnoo - a businessman turned conservationist. The man who took a pledge for zero polythene in Gilsar, Khushalsar, Nigeen and succeeded. Now he is on a new mission - to save Anchaar, a lake he calls an orphan. Once sprawling across nearly 20 square kilometres, Anchar Lake has shrunk to barely 4.5 square kilometres, with a substantial portion of its remaining area reduced to marshland. In this exclusive conversation with Sarosh Kafeel, Manzoor Wangnoo speaks openly about the land mafia encroaching Anchaar, the support from the administration, and how he approached the present government and the CM but got no response. He warns that if Anchaar is not cleaned, Kashmir will face a flood-like situation again. The damage is so big, it will take at least a decade to clean it. His message is clear - youngsters have to come out and save this orphan lake before it's too late. Host: Sarosh Kafeel
